title: Projection Month of the Homeowner's Premium in a Rural Home Loans Escrow Projection
content:
Escrow calendar rule for Rural Home Loans: the month in which the homeowner's insurance premium is projected to fall due.

## Rule

The month in which the homeowner's premium is projected to fall due is chosen as follows: when the homeowner's policy expiry on the loan record falls in the second through the twelfth month of the projection, the months being counted as whole months from the next payment due date, and the month just ahead of that expiry is not the anniversary month of the latest premium bill, the premium falls due in the month just ahead of the expiry; when the expiry on record falls earlier than one whole month past the next payment due date, the premium falls due in the opening month of the projection; otherwise it falls due in the anniversary month of its latest bill.

## Terms

- **Months of the projection:** the opening month is the month of the next payment due date; a date falls in the second month when it is at least one and fewer than two whole months after the next payment due date, and so on through the twelfth.
- **Expiry on record:** the homeowner's insurance expiry date on the loan record.
- **Anniversary month:** the calendar month of the latest homeowner's premium paid from escrow, one year later.

## Points of judgement (hypothetical dates, next payment due 1 November)

| Expiry on record | Month the expiry falls in | Anniversary month | Premium projected in |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15 February | fourth | June | January, the month just ahead of the expiry |
| 10 December | second | May | November, the opening month (the month just ahead of the expiry) |
| 20 October | before one whole month | August | November, the opening month |
| 15 November | before one whole month | August | November, the opening month |
| 5 November of the next year | after the twelfth | March | March, the anniversary month |
